//: Pinned third-party binaries that get BUNDLED into the installer — and, on macOS,
deep-signed with the maintainer's Developer ID and notarized. Until 2026-09 the
macOS ffmpeg was fetched from `/redirect/latest/` with no version and no checksum,
so two releases cut a month apart carried different, unrecorded ffmpeg builds: when
an ffmpeg CVE lands, 'which of our releases is affected?' could only be answered by
unpacking each DMG. The Windows/Linux ffmpeg re-resolved 'newest autobuild' from the
GitHub API on every build, with the same effect.
Every entry here is url + sha256. The fetch scripts refuse a download whose hash
does not match. Bumping a pin is a reviewable diff, which is the whole point.
then take the hash from that same URL + '.sha256' (upstream publishes one).
ffmpeg (BtbN)   gh api repos/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds/releases?per_page=5 — pick the newest
autobuild-* tag; each asset carries a `digest` field (sha256:...).
These MUST stay equal to UV_ARTIFACTS in
self-installs the same release when no sidecar is bundled.

ffmpeg.comment: martin-riedl.de macOS builds are static + notarized and link only against system frameworks (fetch-ffmpeg's assert_portable re-checks that). BtbN win64-gpl/linux64-gpl are static with libass + libx264/x265; dated autobuild-* tags are immutable once published, unlike the rolling `latest` release whose assets are deleted and re-uploaded hourly. Since the 2026-11 refresh Windows/Linux pin the RELEASE-BRANCH build each autobuild also carries (`ffmpeg-n9.0.2-…-gpl-9.0`: the 9.0 stable branch plus its backports) instead of the `ffmpeg-N-…` master snapshot, so all four targets ship the same 9.0.2 stable line. fetch-ffmpeg locates any `ffmpeg-*/bin/` folder, so the different archive name needs no script change.

uv.comment: MIRROR of UV_ARTIFACTS in packages/node-orchestrator/src/engines/uvBootstrap.ts, keyed by Rust triple instead of platform-arch. The version lives in fetch-uv.{sh,ps1} (a unit test keeps it in lockstep with the orchestrator's UV_VERSION); only the hashes live here.
